summary: Built in: GRA's PAYE rates and its GMD 3,000 monthly threshold, NPF at 5% employee and 10% employer on basic salary, and the IICF's 1% capped at GMD 15. Entered by each organisation: the monthly PAYE band limits above the threshold (GRA publishes annual bands), whether NPF is deductible before PAYE, what "total earnings" means for the IICF and when it's due, and whether the organisation is in the Federated Pension Scheme.
Not modelled: fringe benefits tax (Plutus doesn't record benefits in kind) and the expatriate quota (an annual per-person charge).

summary: Built in: the four-band PAYE schedule of Law No. 027/2022 (0%, 10%, 20% and 30%, with cut-offs at RWF 60,000, 100,000 and 200,000 a month; the three-band schedule some guides still show was the law's first year only), RSSB pension on gross pay including transport (6% employee and 6% employer in 2026; 14% in all from 1 January 2027, under Presidential Order No. 086/01 of 2024), RSSB maternity leave at 0.3% from the employer, CBHI at 0.5% of the employee's net pay (RRA, citing Prime Minister's Order No. 034/01 of 2020), and the 15th as the deadline for PAYE, RSSB and CBHI. Entered by each organisation: whether RSSB contributions are deducted before PAYE, the employee's maternity rate (sources disagree), what maternity and occupational hazards are charged on, the occupational hazards rate (sources disagree), and, from 2027, the employee's share of the 14% pension (the order doesn't divide it; the employer pays the rest).
Pension rises again to 16% in January 2028, so 2028 periods are refused until a rule set for 2028 is added.

summary: Ghana, from 1 September 2026 (Income Tax (Amendment) Act 2026, Act 1178).

Built in: the Act 1178 PAYE rates and the GHS 588 monthly threshold, PAYE due on the 15th, and social security at 5.5% employee and 13% employer on basic salary, paid out as the SSNIT Omnibus's worked example pays it: 13.5% to SSNIT (Tier 1) and 5% to the Tier 2 corporate trustee. Entered by each organisation: the monthly PAYE band limits above the threshold (GRA's monthly table wasn't found, and sources disagree where 30% starts), whether SSNIT is deductible before PAYE, the contribution ceiling (sources disagree), and the SSNIT and Tier 2 deadlines.
Periods before 1 September 2026 aren't covered: the earlier schedule wasn't captured, so they're refused.

summary: Built in: the six-band ITS schedule (Ordonnance No. 2023-719, from 2024), its family reduction (RICF: XOF 5,500 a month for each half-share above one share, counting up to five shares), CNPS retirement at 6.3% employee and 7.7% employer, maternity at 0.75% from the employer, and universal health cover (CMU) at XOF 1,000 a month. Entered by each organisation, where no source settles them or sources disagree: what CNPS contributions are charged on, the retirement ceiling, the family benefits rate, the ceiling on family benefits, maternity and work accidents, the employer's work accident rate, the employee's share of CMU, the training levy rates, the employer tax on salaries, and every deadline.

ITS needs each employee's family shares, and the employer tax on salaries whether each is an expatriate: payroll refuses an employee without them. CMU is charged for the employee only; dependants' cover isn't included.
